samples.marker: DNS Beacon x86: C2, thread hijack, header erasure; add coverage

reverse_engineering.identification: Configured x86 reflective DNS Beacon implant
paths: MZRE bootstrap resolves and calls the exported reflective mapper at VA 0x1000a036. The mapper copies sections, fixes imports/relocations and calls the mapped entry point.

DNS loop at 0x1000440d formats DNS names, queries A records, network-decodes and XORs the response, accepts the F0 task word, selects DNS data fetch modes, decrypts/authenticates the received buffer at 0x1000b43b, and dispatches task records at 0x10009ae2.
Task record dispatcher reads network-order command and length fields and routes the payload to the large handler table at 0x10009446. The buffer is wiped after processing.

Remote allocation/write helper 0x100064af calls the memory allocator at 0x1000ca29 and writer at 0x1000d3a3. The execution helpers can create remote threads or rewrite CONTEXT.Eip and resume a suspended thread.
The reflective copy routine clears the NT signature, DOS magic and e_lfanew at 0x1000a5b2.
reverse_engineering.configuration: A 4096-byte configuration block at file offset 0x33a20 XORs with 0x2e into 57 TLV settings: DNS transport, port 53, sleep 10000 ms, a server/path pair, RSA public key, DNS prefixes and spawn targets. These values are evidence, not rule gates.
reverse_engineering.context: Cobalt Strike can serve authorized testing; no engagement authorization or deployment context was supplied. A configured memory-resident task implant with injection and image identification erasure is likely malicious when found on a machine.

samples.marker: DNS Beacon template: tasking and stealth injection; add coverage

paths: The MZRE bootstrap calls ReflectiveLoader at 0x10008b2d. Its code performs image allocation/copy, import resolution, relocation and entry-point handoff.
Contains the same numbered DNS framing and F0 control-word protocol with numeric task dispatch.
The direct-import variant of the context routine initializes CONTEXT_FULL, queries the thread, overwrites Eip at context+0xb0, calls SetThreadContext and resumes the thread.
The mapper erases mapped PE identification headers at 0x1000907b. Remote allocation, writes, APC and remote-thread execution paths are also present.

samples.marker: AES module wrapper: caller-keyed local load; fix false conviction

reverse_engineering.identification: Caller-keyed AES-GCM local Node module wrapper
paths: Importing this module only loads fs/path/crypto, declares helpers and exports validateGraph. It does not itself decrypt or execute a stage at import time.
Calling validateGraph serializes callerData as the password. The embedded 52-byte Base64 envelope is split into 16-byte salt, 12-byte IV, 16-byte authentication tag and 8-byte encrypted module name.
scryptSync derives the 32-byte key; AES-256-GCM with setAuthTag/update/final authenticates and decrypts the name. A wrong caller value throws before file staging.

The name is joined beneath __dirname. materializeModule reads that local file as UTF-8/Base64, decrypts it with the same password, removes an enc_ basename prefix, writes the plaintext, returns its path and require loads that path. The exported function then calls the loaded module's validateGraph.

No network, command execution, persistence, credential targeting or analysis-environment probe is implemented by the supplied source. This statement comes from tracing the complete source, not from a clean scan.
reverse_engineering.context: The caller value and encrypted sibling were not supplied, so the name and downstream behavior remain unresolved. The wrapper is compatible with local encrypted plugin/IP protection. No package manifest, install trigger, deception, payload or other evidence establishes an attack in this artifact. A superficially similar malicious npm fixture is not provenance for these bytes. Retain suspicious caller-keyed code concealment while overturning the hostile conviction.
